testcase.name: cluster.admission-policy

failure.message: the install identity may not create a SecurityContextConstraints: budcluster's apply_security_context step fails at deploy time and the runtime pods stay denied by the default restricted-v2 SCC

testcase.failure: PodSecurity labels and Kyverno/Gatekeeper ClusterPolicies were not inspected: on OpenShift the SCC layer is authoritative and PSA runs in warn/audit grant the install identity SCC authority: `oc create clusterrole budctl-scc --verb=create,get,list,update,patch --resource=securitycontextconstraints.security.openshift.io` then `oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user budctl-scc <identity>`

testcase.name: cluster.installer-rbac

failure.message: this identity cannot create namespaces, customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io, clusterroles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io, clusterrolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io, applicationsets.argoproj.io: the bootstrap stops at the first object it applies and nothing installs

testcase.failure: namespaces — every Application syncs with CreateNamespace=true customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io — Dapr, cert-manager, CNPG and ArgoCD each register CRDs clusterroles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io — the bundled operators install cluster-scoped RBAC clusterrolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io — the bundled operators bind that RBAC to their ServiceAccounts applicationsets.argoproj.io — the install is two ApplicationSets applied by hand bind the install identity to a role that grants them — for a POC, `kubectl create clusterrolebinding budctl-installer --clusterrole=cluster-admin --user=<identity>`; for a scoped role, grant create on namespaces, customresourcedefinitions, clusterroles, clusterrolebindings and applicationsets.argoproj.io

skipped.message: namespace "default" does not exist, so there was nowhere to send a harmless dry-run apply; re-run with a kubeconfig whose context has a default namespace

testcase.name: components.dns

failure.message: no CoreDNS or kube-dns pods in openshift-dns or kube-system: nothing in the cluster can resolve a Service name, so every Dapr service-invocation hop, database connection and object-store call fails

testcase.failure: install the distribution's DNS addon before installing Bud — no chart in either ApplicationSet provides cluster DNS. On kubeadm it arrives with the CNI manifest; on k3s and managed distributions it is present by default, so its absence means the addon was disabled or removed.

testcase.name: components.metrics-server

failure.message: the v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io APIService does not exist: every HPA the chart creates reads `<unknown>/70%` and never scales, so the platform sits at its minimum replica count under any load

testcase.failure: OpenShift serves metrics.k8s.io from the cluster monitoring stack rather than a standalone metrics-server, so this is a broken monitoring stack and not a missing install: `oc get clusteroperator monitoring` and `oc -n openshift-monitoring get pods` show why the aggregated API is gone

testcase.name: storage.capacity

failure.message: provisionable capacity is UNVERIFIED for gp3-csi (ebs.csi.aws.com): the driver publishes no CSIStorageCapacity, there is no OpenEBS DiskPool, and the class is not node-local — required 557 GiB = 200 GiB model weights + 58 GiB platform claims + 269 GiB in-cluster data stores + 30 GiB traces and metrics (30d retention), estimated could be short and the install would fail mid-sync

testcase.failure: budctl will not guess: an unmeasured backend is reported as unknown, not as sufficient check the backend by hand before installing — `vgs` for LVM, `kubectl get diskpool -A` for Mayastor, the cloud console quota for EBS/Azure Disk — and confirm it holds 557 GiB
